This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=efhk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Current meteorological observations and model consensus strongly support the market's near-certain positioning on a 19°C high in Helsinki today.** Official forecasts and real-time data from sources such as GFS indicate mostly clear skies with southwesterly winds allowing afternoon temperatures to peak near or at 19°C (around 66°F), consistent with the day's climatological range of roughly 17–18°C. This aligns with reported afternoon readings hovering at 18°C and limited diurnal variation under stable pressure. Trader consensus reflects this tight clustering of guidance, with minimal divergence in ensemble runs. Only an unexpected rapid cooling from increased cloud cover or a station-specific measurement anomaly at the official Helsinki site could realistically shift the recorded maximum away from 19°C before midnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-pressure dominance and subsidence over the Iberian Peninsula have driven clear skies and southerly flow, positioning Madrid for peak temperatures well above the 29°C September 4 climatological average. Latest GFS and ECMWF model consensus points to afternoon maxima near 38–39°C under minimal cloud cover and light winds, consistent with market-implied odds favoring 39°C at 61.5% and 40°C at 26.5%. These outcomes align with observed heat anomalies persisting into early September, though slight model spread in boundary-layer mixing leaves room for 38°C or a brief push to 40°C. Final resolution will hinge on official AEMET station readings tomorrow, with any last-minute frontal approach capable of trimming the high by 1–2°C.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Historical September 4 averages near 80 °F provide context, but the current warm, humid airmass and weak steering pattern shift the distribution higher than climatology. Updated NWS briefings and hourly mesonet data tomorrow morning will refine the exact maximum before market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eham

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance from METMalaysia point to afternoon highs of 33–35 °C in Kuala Lumpur on September 5, driving the market’s heavy weighting toward 34 °C (56 %) and 35 °C (27 %).** 

In the equatorial climate, September falls in the inter-monsoon period marked by light winds, high humidity, and scattered convection; official outlooks show morning haze transitioning to afternoon thunderstorms that cap extreme heating while still permitting brief peaks near 34 °C under partly cloudy skies. Historical September means hover around 32–33 °C, with the urban heat-island effect in the city center adding 1–2 °C to official airport readings. Recent model consensus and the absence of strong monsoon surges or clear-sky anomalies keep probabilities tightly clustered, though any shift in steering flow or reduced cloud cover before resolution could nudge the highest reading toward 35 °C or hold it at 33 °C. Traders are effectively pricing the narrow uncertainty band typical of short-range tropical forecasts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from agencies including the Met Office and regional sources project a Saturday high near 25–26°C for Mexico City, driven by moderate cloud cover, light winds, and a 30–60% chance of afternoon showers typical of the early-September rainy season at 2,240 m elevation. These conditions limit solar heating and evapotranspiration-driven instability, keeping maxima below seasonal peaks while historical September averages hover around 25°C. Minor model spread in timing of convective clouds versus clearer intervals separates the tightly matched 26°C and 27°C-or-higher outcomes, with fresh ECMWF and GFS runs expected to clarify resolution criteria before the market closes. Trader consensus aligns with this narrow scientific uncertainty.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus clusters tightly around 30–32°C for Panama City’s September 5 high, reflecting the narrow range of outcomes typical for the peak of the wet season.** Persistent ITCZ-driven convection, high humidity near 80–85%, and frequent afternoon thunderstorms tend to cap daytime maxima near the 30–31°C September climatological average, while brief clearer intervals can allow brief spikes to 32°C. A strengthening El Niño, with Niño-3.4 anomalies exceeding +2°C and a >90% chance of a very strong event by fall 2026, adds a modest warm bias that supports the slight market tilt toward the upper end of this band. Resolution hinges on the exact timing and coverage of convection on the 5th, which short-range models update daily.
